question: A patient with vitiligo on the dorsa of the hands requests surgical melanocyte transplantation. What is the essential prerequisite before this can be offered?

answers.text: The disease must be actively spreading so that grafts can repigment new areas as they appear

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Operating on actively spreading vitiligo risks Koebnerisation (new depigmented patches at surgical sites) and graft failure. Active disease is a contraindication to surgery, not an indication.

answers.text: The disease must have been stable — no new lesions and no expansion of existing ones — for at least one year

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Surgical repigmentation procedures require stable disease, defined as no new lesions and no expansion for at least one year (per IADVL guidance). Stability ensures the autoimmune process is quiescent and grafted melanocytes will not be destroyed by ongoing attack.

answers.text: The patient must first complete a full course of depigmentation therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Depigmentation therapy (destroying remaining melanocytes) is a separate option reserved for very extensive, treatment-resistant vitiligo covering more than 50% of BSA, not a prerequisite for surgical repigmentation.

answers.text: Surgery can be offered at any stage regardless of disease activity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Disease stability for at least one year is mandatory because operating on active vitiligo carries a high risk of Koebnerisation at surgical sites and graft failure from ongoing autoimmune melanocyte destruction.

overallFeedback.feedback: Surgical repigmentation requires STABLE disease — at least one year with no new lesions and no expansion (per IADVL guidance). Operating on active disease risks Koebnerisation at surgical sites and destruction of grafted melanocytes by ongoing autoimmune attack.

Correct. Stability is the gatekeeper for surgical vitiligo treatment — at least one year of no new lesions and no expansion ensures the autoimmune process is quiescent and grafted melanocytes can survive.
